note: D-H3. The shared table for the two implementations that decide whether an import specifier
The engine path is the primary one and the TypeScript regex is the degraded fallback it
replaced, so the containment must run one way: anything the fallback catches, the engine
catches. It did not. The fallback has recognised drizzle|typeorm|sequelize since it was
written and the engine recognised only prisma|database|db|data-access, which is how a repo
whose data layer is Drizzle got told it has no data layer at all.
Where the engine is deliberately NARROWER it must say so in narrowing_reason. That is the
whole mechanism: a narrowing with a reason is a decision, a narrowing without one is the
D-H3 defect coming back. Both crates/drift-engine/tests/data_access_vocabulary.rs and
packages/cli/test/data-access-vocabulary.test.ts assert this table; add a case to the table
and both sides pick it up.
